_rationale: While both spouses are alive (indices 0–7), household Social Security = 40k + 25k = 65k. The spouse dies at age 72 (offset 7), so survivor mode begins at index 8: from then on the household keeps only the larger benefit, max(40k, 25k) = 40k. Roth-only portfolio means no RMDs and no Traditional/brokerage withdrawals muddy the income. The projection runs the full self horizon (index 25 = age 90). Probability is 100%: $1M Roth + $40–65k SS easily covers $50k/yr spending with 0% growth, so the portfolio never depletes.

breakdownChecks._note: Both alive: household SS is the SUM of both benefits
Year of the spouse's death: still MFJ, still both benefits
Survivor year: only the LARGER benefit (40k) survives — widow's penalty
Survivor benefit persists for the rest of the survivor's life
